Each degree is divided by the four nodes on the other side, so F, linked to B, C and D, scores 0.75, E 0.50 and G 0.25." width="100%"} In a bipartite graph a node can only connect to nodes on the *other* side, so its largest possible degree is the size of the opposite partition, not `n - 1` as in an ordinary graph. This method scores each node in the chosen partition by its degree divided by the size of the opposite partition. A score of `1.0` means the node is linked to every node on the other side; `0.5` means it is linked to half of them. The partitions are those returned by `bipartite_sets()`. Because of this normalization, scores are comparable across the two sides of the graph even when they differ greatly in size. Typical questions it answers: - which members attend the largest share of events (or events attract the largest share of members)? - which genes are linked to the most diseases, relative to how many diseases there are? - which products are bought by the largest fraction of customers? Only nodes in the chosen partition are scored. Degree is the number of incident edges, so in a multigraph each parallel edge counts and scores can exceed `1.0`. If the opposite partition is empty (e.g. a graph with no edges), every score is `0.0`. On a directed graph edge direction is ignored, so the degree is in-degree plus out-degree. The whole graph is used and the current selection is ignored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [which]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which partition to compute centrality for: `0` (default) or `1`. Partitions are numbered as in `bipartite_sets()`: in each connected component, partition `0` is the side that contains the component's lowest node ID. Any other value raises an error. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node DataFrame column the scores are written to. If `None` (default), the column is named `"bipartite_degree_centrality"`. Only nodes in the chosen partition are written: if the column is new, the other nodes get null values; if it already exists, their existing values are kept. This lets you fill one column for both sides by calling the method twice with the same `attr_name=` (see the examples). [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `False` (default), returns the graph itself so calls can be chained, and records the computation so it is listed by `describe()`. If `True`, returns the scores as a dictionary instead, without writing anything to the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping each node ID in the chosen partition to its score (normally in the range `[0, 1]`). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): the graph itself, for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is not bipartite, or if `which=` is not `0` or `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In this small people-film network, the people are partition `0` and the films are partition `1`. "Film2" was watched by three of the four people, so it scores `0.75`, while "Film3" (one viewer) scores `0.25`: ::: {#15ffa459 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["Ann", "Bob", "Cal", "Dee", "Film1", "Film2", "Film3"]) .add_edges( [ ("Ann", "Film1"), ("Bob", "Film1"), ("Bob", "Film2"), ("Cal", "Film2"), ("Cal", "Film3"), ("Dee", "Film2"), ] ) ) scores = graph.bipartite_degree_centrality(which=1, return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): score for nid, score in sorted(scores.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'Film1': 0.5, 'Film2': 0.75, 'Film3': 0.25} ``` ::: ::: On the people side the denominator is the three films, so "Bob" and "Cal" (two films each) score `2/3` and the others `1/3`. Calling the method for both partitions with the same `attr_name=` fills a single column covering every node: ::: {#c58200e1 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( graph .bipartite_degree_centrality(which=0, attr_name="bip_degree") .bipartite_degree_centrality(which=1, attr_name="bip_degree") .get_node_df() .select(["label", "bip_degree"]) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
